from_quote: As the ſenators are ſtill to be elected by the legiſlatures of the ſtates
rationale: The paragraph says that senators "are still to be elected by the legislatures of the states," which restates Article I, Section 3, Clause 1.

from_quote: Impeachments alone are the caſes cognizable before them
rationale: The paragraph says that impeachments are the cases the Senate tries, and goes on to the two-thirds vote and the oath, all of which are in Article I, Section 3, Clause 6.
to_quote: The Senate shall have the sole Power to try all Impeachments

from_quote: the people, who alone can impeach him by their immediate repreſentatives
rationale: The paragraph says the people "alone can impeach" through "their immediate representatives," which names the House's power of impeachment in Article I, Section 2, Clause 5.

from_quote: nor can they join in making proviſion for themſelves, either by creating new places, or encreaſing the emoluments of old ones
rationale: The paragraph says senators cannot hold another office or create new places or increase the emoluments of old ones, which describes Article I, Section 6, Clause 2.
to_quote: the Emoluments whereof shall have been encreased during such time

from_quote: The judges of the foederal courts will owe their appointments to the preſident and ſenate
rationale: The paragraph says the federal judges are appointed by the President and Senate, the appointment power in Article II, Section 2, Clause 2.
to_quote: shall appoint Ambassadors, other public Ministers and Consuls, Judges of the supreme Court

from_quote: till thirty years have ripened his abilities
rationale: The paragraph says no one can sit in the Senate until he is thirty, the age qualification in Article I, Section 3, Clause 3.
to_quote: attained to the Age of thirty Years

from_quote: the public treaſures, the ſinews of the ſtate, cannot be called forth by their original motion
rationale: The paragraph says the Senate cannot originate measures to raise the public treasure and so describes the origination clause of Article I, Section 7, Clause 1.
to_quote: All Bills for raising Revenue shall originate in the House of Representatives

from_quote: They can only, by conviction on impeachment, remove and incapacitate a dangerous officer, but the puniſhment of him as a criminal remains within the province of the courts of law
rationale: The paragraph describes conviction on impeachment as removal and disqualification, with punishment as a criminal left to the courts, which is the content of Article I, Section 3, Clause 7.
to_quote: Judgment in Cases of Impeachment shall not extend further than to removal from Office

from_quote: having a ſeparate and independent vote
rationale: The paragraph says each senator has "a separate and independent vote" and that "there are only two" from each state, which are the provisions of Article I, Section 3, Clause 1.
to_quote: each Senator shall have one Vote

from_quote: The ſenate muſt always receive the exceptions of the preſident againſt any of their legiſlatve acts
rationale: The paragraph says the Senate must receive the President's "exceptions" to its acts, which describes the return of bills with objections in Article I, Section 7, Clause 2.
to_quote: he shall return it, with his Objections to that House in which it shall have originated
